topic.topic: South Sea Bubble and Isaac Newton
topic.angle: Even Newton lost money in a bubble

panels.text: The South Sea Company was founded in 1711 to reduce the size of public debts. In 1720, its stock peaked, then collapsed in what became the South Sea Bubble.
Sir Isaac Newton owns nearly £22,000 in South Sea stock, and loses at least £10,000.
He is quoted: "I can calculate the movement of the stars, but not the madness of men".

claims.claim: In 1720, its stock peaked, then collapsed.
claims.quote: Company stock rose greatly in value as it expanded its operations dealing in government debt, and peaked in 1720 before suddenly collapsing to little above its original flotation price.

claims.claim: The collapse became known as the South Sea Bubble.
claims.quote: The notorious economic bubble this created, which ruined thousands of investors, became known as the South Sea Bubble
